But unfortunately for you, and all of us, that is not the case. Each name goes to a committee that checks the background of the person, holds hearings, may even make analysis and report findings as to why or why not this person should not be confirmed. They may even flat out refuse to act altogether.

This happens before the entire Senate is involved. If the committees refuse to act, the Senate can take over the confirmation process of that particular nominee and call for vote. But if even one member of that committee objects, then the confirmation process goes back to the committee (who refused to act in the first place). Only after the committee either finishes their process or refuses to object, does the entire Senate vote.

This, my simple friend, is why the confirmation of judges takes a long time.
